# Thothica

> Hard problems can be solved when people understand their data. Thothica helps them do that by building ontologies and AI-native software. Thothica is an AI startup: it builds ontologies, and software on top of them, so staff and AI systems work from the same definitions of an organization's data, and the organization no longer depends on only a few experienced people to interpret it.

Thothica (legal name: Thothica Private Limited) is an AI startup based in New Delhi, India, founded in 2023. Its discipline is data ontology. Contact: hello@thothica.com. This file describes the single-page site so that LLMs and crawlers can understand it without rendering the page.

## What Thothica does

Every organization has people who know how to answer the difficult questions. They know which reports are wrong, which database column actually matters, why two departments use different names for the same thing, and how an approval really works.

An ontology is that knowledge, written down precisely enough that software can run on it. Today it lives in a few people's heads.

Thothica writes it down for whatever system a client already runs, in whatever field they work in.

Thothica's software reads a client's systems and writes the first version of the ontology. It works out what each item means, how the items relate to one another, and who decides. Thothica sets the rules it follows and checks its work. The client's staff and AI can then both ask it questions, and every answer shows which record it came from.

The organization no longer depends on only a few experienced people to interpret its data. It can solve, at scale, the problems those people used to solve one at a time.

## What an ontology is made of

An ontology has three parts. Together, these three are the ontology, written down in one place and one structure, so that people and software read the same thing.

- **Data sources, what you have.** Scanned PDFs, spreadsheets and CSV files, databases, legacy systems, SAP and other enterprise software. It does not matter where the data sits; Thothica's software writes the connection to each source, so nothing has to be moved or typed in again.
- **Logic sources, what you know.** Formulas buried in spreadsheets, existing code, machine learning models, written rules and prompts. Some of it is in no system at all: it sits with the people who have done the job for years. Thothica sends in forward deployed agents, software that works alongside a client's experts, asks them how the job is really done, and writes the answers down in the same structure as everything else.
- **Systems of action, what you do.** An ERP, existing portals, a new system Thothica builds, or an AI agent. Thothica builds the system the client acts in, or puts the layer inside the one they already use, so a decision arrives as a step someone can take.

## Case studies

Full write-ups live at https://thothica.com/case-studies/, one page per system, each with diagrams.

- **Five live government portals** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/government-portals/). Thothica built the AI layer that now runs on five state government portals, each built on a different technology and each storing its data differently. For each portal Thothica first wrote down what its data measures and every way it can legitimately be broken down (by district, by scheme, by month, by status), then classified the portal's free-text fields into a fixed set so they could be counted. On one portal that classification made 115,652 separate decisions about what a piece of text meant. An official asks a question in plain language and gets an answer taken from that portal's own records, with every figure traceable back to the rows it came from. The layer holds read permission only and cannot alter a record. Across all five the method did not change; the catalogue content did.
- **A think tank's historical archive** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/think-tank-archive/). More than 1,000 primary works from an intellectual tradition going back to the 1850s, held as more than 2,000 PDFs that were mostly photographs of printed pages on a slow website. Thothica's software turned the pictures into text across five languages and several scripts, then built the ontology in four layers: works (document type, series, position in a run), people (506 writers resolved to one identity each across scripts, spellings and initials), relations (who wrote what, who is the subject of what, who is mentioned inside what, who argued with whom), and positions (where each writer sits in the tradition on several independent axes). Every relation carries the verbatim passage that proves it, checked as a substring of the source text; a relation whose quotation fails that check is discarded rather than kept with a warning, so a fabricated quotation cannot survive storage. Roughly three quarters of writers came out of the first classification pass flagged for human review. The archive is split into two declared tiers: clean text that software may quote directly with paragraph-level addresses, and scanned works that software must describe and link out to rather than quote.
- **A publisher's comic production line** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/comic-production/). For one of India's largest publishers, a research corpus of roughly ten million words (70+ books converted and chaptered, 220+ interviews transcribed) organized on one ontology: Line, Program, Subject, then Dossier as input and Comic as output. Sources are split chapter-per-file so a claim can point at an exact file and line, which is what makes the citation contract mechanically checkable rather than a slogan. Because every subject's research sits in one corpus, the library already holds passages where other people describe this subject; finding them uses entity anchoring (the name, its likely mangled forms, and the person's companies, teams and signature events) with the speaker confirmed from content rather than from a speaker label, because transcripts garble names and mislabel speakers. Every beat in a finished script carries a pointer to its source line, and a gate resolves each pointer before the script proceeds. Hundreds of comic books have been drafted this way.
- **An unattended newsroom for a sports media publisher** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/cricket-content-engine/). An engine that reads live match data, the news wire and fan forums, plans its own slate, writes in the publisher's voice against a written style specification, corroborates its claims against sources it actually fetches, and then stops at a private editorial queue where a human decides what runs. Its taxonomy is a declared ontology in one manifest that every consumer reads from; each dimension states its kind, whether an item may carry one value or several, and what happens to an unfamiliar value: closed dimensions fail the build, curated dimensions warn, and auto-grow dimensions accept and queue for curation so coverage of a debut is never blocked. Aliases resolve every known form of a name to one identity so counts cannot fragment. The engine holds only a data-read key and push access to one repository; it holds no credential that can publish to the public site.
- **An academic olympiad's handwritten registrations** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/olympiad-forms/). Schools submit registrations on pre-printed grids and hand-ruled registers. The doctrine is that the model does perception and the code does arithmetic: a vision model transcribes what is on the paper, and every sum, reconciliation and verdict is computed deterministically afterwards. The independence rule follows: evidence that confirms a reading must come from a source independent of it, so a total read in the same pass may contradict the marks but may never confirm them. The handwritten total is read again separately and voted on, then pinned so a later repair cannot rewrite the number it is measured against. Absence of evidence is never green: a sheet with no usable checksum is reported as unverified, not as a match. Paper that contradicts itself is flagged, never silently repaired. The guarantee is not perfect accuracy but that nothing wrong ships silently.

## Use cases

- AI layers integrated into legacy software. The existing system stays exactly as it is. Thothica reads its database and writes down what its tables and columns mean in the words staff actually use, and the layer sits on top of that. Staff ask questions in plain language instead of opening many screens and exporting spreadsheets, and every number reported can be traced back to the data it came from.
- Approval systems for governments. Before writing software, Thothica writes down what each scheme requires: which document proves which condition, which officer signs at which stage, and what makes an application complete. The software then checks every application against that record. The applicant sees exactly what is missing; the official sees which files are ready for a decision and which are stuck and why.

## Open source

- Falsafa.ai (https://falsafa.ai), Thothica's open-source library of the world's philosophical, classical and religious texts. It holds more than 2,000 works, divided into more than 1.3 million passages that can each be quoted and cited exactly. On top of the library Thothica builds the Atlas, a map of the collection drawn from the texts themselves: it records the people, ideas, places, groups, events and objects that appear across twenty-five centuries of writing, and every time one text cites another it records how, whether the later author treated the earlier one as an authority, agreed with it, extended it, or argued against it. Every entry is tied to a paragraph that can be read in place. The software that builds the Atlas cannot write quotations; it only points at paragraphs, and the words are attached afterwards from the source text, so an invented quotation is impossible.

## Why the method repeats

The same software does all of it. On one government portal it made 115,652 decisions about what the data meant. In a historical archive it read more than 1,000 works and recorded who was mentioned in each one, on what subject and in what context. For a publisher it has drafted hundreds of comic books on its own, researching each one first and citing a real source on every line.

Five government portals. An archive of scanned documents in five languages. A library of more than 2,000 works spanning twenty-five centuries. A publisher's research and production line. Every one of them stored its data differently, and no two were in the same business. Thothica's way of working did not change once. There is more running now that has not been announced.

Thothica works with some of India's largest publishers, with state governments, and with leading think tanks and small businesses.

Tell Thothica your hardest problem. It will solve it.
